items.vi: Giới thiệu bản thân
items.p: Write a short message to your new pen friend. Tell them your name, age, where you live and what you like.
items.pv: Viết tin nhắn ngắn cho người bạn qua thư mới. Nói tên, tuổi, nơi bạn sống và điều bạn thích.
c: Ít nhất hai điều bạn thích
Câu kết (hỏi lại bạn ấy hoặc chào tạm biệt)
m: Hi! My name is Lan and I am nineteen years old. I live in Hai Phong, a big city in Vietnam. I like music and I love cooking. I also like swimming in the sea. What about you? Write soon!

items.vi: Gia đình tôi
items.p: Write a message to a friend about your family. How many people are there? What do they do?
items.pv: Viết tin nhắn cho bạn về gia đình bạn. Nhà bạn có mấy người? Mọi người làm gì?
c: Ít nhất hai người và công việc của họ
Một điều bạn thích làm cùng gia đình
u: There are … people in my family
m: Hi Tom! There are four people in my family. My father is a taxi driver and my mother works in a hospital. My little brother is a student. We often eat dinner together and watch TV on Sunday because it is our free day.

items.vi: Thiệp mời sinh nhật
items.p: Write an invitation to your birthday party. Say the day, the time and the place.
items.pv: Viết lời mời đến tiệc sinh nhật của bạn. Nói ngày, giờ và địa điểm.
c: Một chi tiết thêm (mang gì, ăn gì…)
u: Please come to my birthday party
Mời bạn đến tiệc sinh nhật của tôi
m: Hi Mai! Please come to my birthday party. It is on Saturday at six o'clock at my house, 12 Le Loi Street. We have pizza, cake and games, so please bring your guitar. See you there! Hoa

items.vi: Bưu thiếp kỳ nghỉ
items.p: You are on holiday. Write a postcard to your teacher. Where are you? What is the weather like? What do you do every day?
items.pv: Bạn đang đi nghỉ. Viết bưu thiếp cho thầy cô. Bạn ở đâu? Thời tiết thế nào? Hằng ngày bạn làm gì?
m: Dear Ms Linh, I am in Nha Trang with my family. The weather is sunny and hot. Every day I swim in the sea and eat fresh fish. The hotel is small but nice. See you next week! Best wishes, Nam

items.vi: Một ngày của tôi
items.p: Write about your day. What time do you get up? What do you do in the morning, afternoon and evening?
items.pv: Viết về một ngày của bạn. Bạn dậy lúc mấy giờ? Sáng, chiều, tối bạn làm gì?
c: Việc buổi sáng, buổi chiều, buổi tối
m: I get up at six o'clock. In the morning I have breakfast and go to school by bike. In the afternoon I study at the library. After that I play football with my friends. In the evening I do my homework, then I go to bed at ten.

items.vi: Cuối tuần vừa rồi
items.p: Write an email to a friend about what you did last weekend. Where did you go? Who were you with? Did you enjoy it?
items.pv: Viết email cho bạn kể cuối tuần vừa rồi bạn làm gì. Bạn đi đâu? Đi với ai? Có vui không?
c: Mở đầu thân mật và lý do viết
Đi đâu, với ai (dùng quá khứ đơn)
m: Hi Minh, How are you? Last weekend I went to Ha Long Bay with my cousins. We took a boat trip and visited a big cave. When we arrived, the weather was cold, but the views were beautiful.
It was really fun, but I was very tired on Sunday evening. What did you do at the weekend? Write back soon. See you soon, Lan

items.vi: Trả lời lời mời
items.genre: tin nhắn trả lời lời mời
items.p: Your friend invited you to a picnic on Sunday, but you can't go. Write a message. Say sorry, explain why and suggest another day.
items.pv: Bạn của bạn mời đi dã ngoại Chủ nhật, nhưng bạn không đi được. Viết tin nhắn: xin lỗi, giải thích lý do và đề nghị ngày khác.
c: Xin lỗi và lý do không đi được
u: Cảm ơn cậu đã mời mình
Mình thật sự xin lỗi, nhưng
m: Hi Hoa, Thanks for inviting me to the picnic. I'm really sorry, but I can't come on Sunday because my grandmother is visiting us.
How about next Saturday? We could go to the park near the lake and bring some sandwiches. Let me know if that is OK for you. Love, Mai

items.vi: Nơi tôi thích nhất
items.p: Write about your favourite place in your town. Where is it? What does it look like? Why do you like it?
items.pv: Viết về nơi bạn thích nhất trong thị trấn/thành phố. Nó ở đâu? Trông thế nào? Vì sao bạn thích?
c: Tên và vị trí nơi đó
m: My favourite place is a small café near my school. It is quiet and there are lots of plants and old books. The coffee is cheap and the music is soft.
I often go there after class with my friends. We do our homework and chat. I like it because it is calm and I can relax after a long day.

items.vi: Hỏi về khoá học tiếng Anh
items.p: You want to join an English course. Write an email to the school. Ask about the time, the price and the teachers.
items.pv: Bạn muốn học một khoá tiếng Anh. Viết email cho trung tâm, hỏi về giờ học, học phí và giáo viên.
c: Chào và nói bạn là ai, bạn muốn gì
Ít nhất ba câu hỏi (giờ, giá, giáo viên)
u: I am writing to ask about
Tôi viết thư để hỏi về
Cảm ơn sự giúp đỡ của anh/chị
m: Dear Sir or Madam, My name is Tuan and I am writing to ask about your evening English course. I work during the day, so I can only study after six o'clock.
Could you tell me what time the classes start? How much does it cost for three months? Are the teachers native speakers? Thank you for your help. Best regards, Tuan

items.vi: Một ngày tồi tệ
items.p: Write a diary entry about a bad day. What happened? How did you feel? What happened in the end?
items.pv: Viết một trang nhật ký về một ngày tồi tệ. Chuyện gì đã xảy ra? Bạn cảm thấy thế nào? Cuối cùng ra sao?
c: Chuyện đầu tiên không suôn sẻ
Các việc tiếp theo, theo thứ tự (first, then, after that)
m: Today was a terrible day. First, my alarm didn't ring and I woke up late. Then it started to rain when I was on my bike, and I got very wet. After that I forgot my homework at home.
I felt angry and sad. Finally, in the evening, my sister made my favourite soup and we watched a funny film. Tomorrow will be better!

items.vi: Ghi chú cho bạn cùng nhà
items.p: You are going out. Write a note to your flatmate. Say where you are going, when you will be back and ask them to do one thing for you.
items.pv: Bạn sắp ra ngoài. Viết ghi chú cho bạn cùng nhà: bạn đi đâu, mấy giờ về, và nhờ bạn ấy làm một việc.
m: Hi Tom, I'm going to the supermarket and then to the gym. I'll be back at seven o'clock. Can you please water the plants? They are in the kitchen. Thanks! Lan

items.vi: Nhà của tôi
items.p: Write about your house or flat. Where is it? How many rooms are there? What is your favourite room and why?
items.pv: Viết về nhà hoặc căn hộ của bạn: ở đâu, có mấy phòng, bạn thích phòng nào nhất và vì sao.
m: I live in a small flat in Da Nang. There are three rooms: a living room, a bedroom and a kitchen. My favourite room is the kitchen because it is big and sunny, and I love cooking.

items.vi: Hồ sơ trao đổi ngôn ngữ
items.p: Write a short profile for a language exchange website. Say your name, age, job, the languages you speak, your hobbies and what you want to learn.
items.pv: Viết hồ sơ ngắn trên trang trao đổi ngôn ngữ: tên, tuổi, nghề, ngôn ngữ bạn nói, sở thích và điều bạn muốn học.
m: Hello! My name is Minh and I am twenty-two. I am a nurse in Hanoi. I speak Vietnamese and a little English. I like football and music. I want to practise speaking English because I want to make new friends.

items.vi: Chỉ đường đến nhà tôi
items.p: A friend is coming to your house for the first time. Write an email. Tell them how to get there from the bus stop and what time to come.
items.pv: Một người bạn lần đầu đến nhà bạn. Viết email chỉ đường từ trạm xe buýt và hẹn giờ đến.
c: Giờ hẹn và lời chào cuối
m:
Hi Anna,

I'm really happy you can come on Saturday! Get off the bus at the post office. First, walk straight on for two minutes. Then turn left at the pharmacy. My house is the yellow one, and it's opposite a small park.

Please come at about six o'clock, because my mum is cooking dinner for us. If you get lost, just call me. See you on Saturday!

Love,
Hoa

items.vi: Một ngày may mắn
items.p: Write a short story about a lucky day. What happened? Where were you? How did you feel at the end?
items.pv: Viết một câu chuyện ngắn về một ngày may mắn. Chuyện gì xảy ra? Bạn ở đâu? Cuối cùng bạn cảm thấy thế nào?
c: Bối cảnh: khi nào, ở đâu
m: Last year I was late for an important job interview. It was raining and I couldn't find a taxi, so I started to walk. Suddenly, a woman on a motorbike stopped and offered to take me to the office.
When I arrived, I saw the same woman in the interview room. She was the manager! I couldn't believe it. She smiled and said I was very polite. In the end, I got the job.

items.vi: Em đã nghỉ học
items.p: You were ill and missed your English class yesterday. Write an email to your teacher. Say sorry, explain why and ask about the homework.
items.pv: Hôm qua bạn ốm nên nghỉ lớp tiếng Anh. Viết email cho giáo viên: xin lỗi, giải thích lý do và hỏi bài tập về nhà.
c: Lời cảm ơn và ký tên
u: Em xin lỗi vì đã nghỉ
Thầy/cô có thể cho em biết
m:
Dear Ms Hanh,

I'm sorry I missed the class yesterday. I had a high temperature and the doctor told me to stay at home. I feel much better today, so I can come to the next lesson.

Could you tell me what the homework is? I also want to know which pages you studied, because I would like to read them before Thursday. Thank you for your help.

Best wishes,
Nam

items.vi: Email cảm ơn và kể chuyện
items.p: You stayed with an English-speaking friend's family last month. Write an email to your friend. Thank the family, say what you enjoyed most, and invite your friend to visit you.
items.pv: Bạn đã ở nhà gia đình một người bạn nói tiếng Anh tháng trước. Viết email cảm ơn, kể điều thích nhất, và mời bạn ấy đến chơi.
c: Lời mời và gợi ý thời gian
u: Cảm ơn bạn rất nhiều vì
Hope to hear from you soon
m: Hi Emma,
Thank you so much for having me last month. Please say a big thank you to your parents too. They made me feel like part of the family.
The best part was the day we spent at the lake. I'd never been kayaking before, and I loved it, even though I fell in twice! Your mum's apple cake was amazing as well.

Would you like to come and stay with us in Hanoi next summer? I could show you the Old Quarter, and we could go to Ha Long Bay for a couple of days. July would be a good time, because I'll be on holiday.
Hope to hear from you soon.

Love,
Linh

items.vi: Truyện: Lên nhầm xe buýt
items.p: Write a story that begins with this sentence: "As soon as the bus left, Nam realised he had made a mistake."
items.pv: Viết truyện mở đầu bằng câu: “Ngay khi xe buýt chạy, Nam nhận ra mình đã nhầm.”
c: Chuyện gì đã xảy ra (quá khứ)
m: As soon as the bus left, Nam realised he had made a mistake. It was going in the opposite direction from his job interview, which started in forty minutes.

At first, he panicked. He didn't know the area, and his phone battery was almost empty. Suddenly, an old woman sitting next to him asked if he was all right. When he explained, she smiled and told him to get off at the next stop and take a motorbike taxi.
Luckily, the driver knew a shortcut. Nam arrived just two minutes late, out of breath but smiling.
In the end, he got the job. On his first day, he discovered that the old woman was his new boss's mother.
k: as soon as the bus left

items.vi: Bài báo: Sở thích của tôi
items.genre: bài báo cho tạp chí trường
items.p: Your school magazine wants articles about hobbies. Write an article about a hobby you enjoy. Say how you started, why you like it and why other students should try it.
items.pv: Tạp chí trường cần bài về sở thích. Viết bài: bạn bắt đầu thế nào, vì sao thích, vì sao bạn khác nên thử.
c: Tiêu đề / câu mở hấp dẫn
u: What I love about it is
Điều tôi thích ở nó là
Why not give it a try?
m: Why Everyone Should Try Rock Climbing
Have you ever wanted to feel like a superhero? Then try rock climbing!
I first started two years ago, when a friend took me to an indoor climbing centre. I was terrified of heights, and I couldn't even reach the top of the easiest wall.
What I love about it is that it exercises your body and your mind at the same time. You have to plan every move, like a puzzle. It's also very social, because climbers always help each other.
You don't need to be strong or fit to begin. Most centres have beginner classes. Why not give it a try?

items.vi: Email hỏi trường ngôn ngữ
items.p: You saw an advertisement for an English summer course in Australia. Write an email to the school. Ask about the length of the course, the accommodation and the cost, and say why you are interested.
items.pv: Bạn thấy quảng cáo khoá tiếng Anh hè ở Úc. Viết email hỏi thời gian khoá, chỗ ở, chi phí, và nói vì sao bạn quan tâm.
c: Lời chào trang trọng, lý do viết
Hỏi thời gian, chỗ ở, chi phí
u: I am writing to ask about
Tôi viết thư để hỏi về
Tôi đặc biệt quan tâm vì
I look forward to hearing from you.
m: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to ask about the English summer course that I saw advertised on your website.
I am particularly interested because I hope to study at an Australian university next year, and I need to improve my academic English.

Could you please tell me how many weeks the course lasts and how many hours of lessons there are each day? I would also like to know whether you can arrange accommodation with a local family. Finally, could you tell me the total cost, including accommodation?
I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Tran Minh Anh

items.vi: Bài luận: Giao thông công cộng
items.p: In your English class you have been discussing transport in cities. Write an essay: "Public transport should be free for everyone. Do you agree?" Write about cost, the environment, and one idea of your own.
items.pv: Viết bài luận: “Giao thông công cộng nên miễn phí cho mọi người. Bạn có đồng ý?” Bàn về chi phí, môi trường, và một ý của riêng bạn.
u: One argument in favour is that
Một lý lẽ ủng hộ là
However, it is also true that
m: Traffic jams and air pollution are serious problems in many cities, and some people believe that making public transport free would help to solve them.

One argument against the idea is cost. Buses and trains are expensive to run, and if passengers do not pay, the money must come from taxes. However, the government already spends huge amounts on building roads and treating illnesses caused by pollution.
As for the environment, free transport would encourage people to leave their motorbikes and cars at home, which would reduce both emissions and noise.
Another point is fairness. People on low incomes spend a large part of their salary on travel, so free buses would make a real difference to their lives.
In conclusion, I believe that free public transport is a good idea, but only if the service is reliable. Free buses that never arrive will not change anyone's habits.

items.vi: Bài nhận xét: một nhà hàng
items.p: A travel website wants reviews of restaurants in your area. Write a review of a restaurant you have been to. Describe the food, the service and the atmosphere, and say who you would recommend it to.
items.pv: Viết bài nhận xét một nhà hàng bạn từng đến: món ăn, phục vụ, không khí, và hợp với ai.
u: The highlight of the meal was
Điểm sáng của bữa ăn là
I would thoroughly recommend it to
m: Tucked away in a small lane in Hue's old town, Ngoc Lan Garden is easy to miss, but it is well worth searching for.

The menu focuses on traditional royal dishes, beautifully presented on small plates. The highlight of the meal was a delicate rice-flour cake steamed in banana leaves, served with a spicy shrimp sauce. Portions are fairly small, so it's best to order several dishes and share.

The staff were friendly and happy to explain each dish, although service became rather slow when the restaurant filled up. The atmosphere is calm and romantic, with tables arranged around a lotus pond and soft traditional music in the background. The only downside was the mosquitoes, so bring some repellent.

I would thoroughly recommend it to couples and to visitors who want to try something more refined than street food. It's not the cheapest option in town, but it is definitely one of the most memorable.

items.vi: Báo cáo: cải thiện căng-tin
items.p: Your principal has asked you to write a report on the school canteen. Describe the current situation, explain what students think, and make recommendations for improvement.
items.pv: Hiệu trưởng nhờ bạn viết báo cáo về căng-tin: hiện trạng, ý kiến học sinh, đề xuất cải thiện.
c: Mục đích báo cáo (có tiêu đề mục)
u: The aim of this report is to
Mục đích của báo cáo này là
Phần lớn học sinh cho rằng
m:
Introduction
The aim of this report is to describe the current situation in the school canteen and to suggest ways of improving it.

Current situation
The canteen serves around 600 students every day. The menu changes only once a month, and there are very few vegetarian options. At lunchtime, queues are often fifteen minutes long.

Students' opinions
According to a survey of 120 students, most feel that the food is too oily and too expensive for the portion size. However, many praised the friendly staff and the clean dining area. Several students also said they would like more fruit and fresh juice instead of fizzy drinks.

Recommendations
It is recommended that the canteen introduces a weekly menu with at least two healthy and vegetarian dishes each day. In addition, a second serving counter could be opened at lunchtime to reduce queues. Finally, students could be invited to vote on new dishes each term.

items.vi: Thư khiếu nại trang trọng
items.p: You recently bought a laptop online, but it arrived late and damaged. Write a letter to the company explaining what happened, how it affected you, and what you would like them to do.
items.pv: Bạn mua laptop trên mạng nhưng giao trễ và hỏng. Viết thư trình bày việc xảy ra, ảnh hưởng tới bạn và bạn muốn công ty làm gì.
c: Mở thư trang trọng, lý do viết
Yêu cầu cụ thể, kết thư
u: I am writing to complain about
Tôi viết thư để khiếu nại về
I would therefore like you to
Vì vậy tôi đề nghị quý công ty
m: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to complain about a laptop I ordered from your website on 2 March (order number 48213).

Your website promised delivery within three days, but the laptop did not arrive until 14 March. To make matters worse, when I opened the box, I discovered that the screen was cracked and the laptop would not switch on.

As a result, I was unable to complete an important assignment on time, and I had to borrow a computer from a friend for over a week. This also caused me considerable stress during an already busy exam period.
I would therefore like you to collect the damaged laptop and either replace it immediately or give me a full refund. I would also appreciate some compensation for the inconvenience caused.
I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Thi Hoa

items.vi: Bài luận: ưu tiên ngân sách
items.p: Your class has attended a panel discussion on how local governments should spend money. Write an essay discussing two of the following priorities: public parks, sports facilities, libraries. Explain which is more important and give reasons.
items.pv: Viết bài luận bàn hai trong ba ưu tiên: công viên, cơ sở thể thao, thư viện. Giải thích cái nào quan trọng hơn, có lý do.
c: Mở bài: bối cảnh, hai ưu tiên chọn
Kết luận: chọn cái nào, vì sao
u: With limited budgets, local authorities face
Với ngân sách hạn chế, chính quyền địa phương đối mặt
A strong case can be made for
Có thể đưa ra lập luận mạnh cho
On balance, I would argue that
Cân nhắc lại, tôi cho rằng
m: With limited budgets, local authorities face difficult choices about which public services to prioritise. Two areas that are frequently discussed are public parks and libraries, both of which serve the whole community rather than a particular group.

A strong case can be made for parks. In densely populated cities, they are often the only green spaces available to residents, offering room for exercise, relaxation and social contact. Research consistently links access to green space with better physical and mental health, and trees also help reduce urban heat and pollution. Parks also host festivals, markets and community events, which strengthen neighbourhood ties in ways that are difficult to measure but easy to recognise.

Libraries, meanwhile, are sometimes dismissed as outdated in the digital age. Admittedly, fewer people borrow printed books than in the past. Yet modern libraries do far more than lend books: they provide free internet access, quiet study space and courses for people of all ages. For low-income families in particular, they can be a vital route to education and employment. In many neighbourhoods, the library is also one of the few warm, safe places where elderly residents can spend the day without being expected to buy anything.

On balance, I would argue that parks should take priority, since their benefits reach almost every resident regardless of age or background. That said, the most effective strategy might be to combine the two, for instance by creating reading spaces within parks, so that limited funds achieve the greatest possible impact.

items.vi: Đề xuất: chương trình sức khoẻ nhân viên
items.p: Your manager has asked for proposals to improve staff wellbeing. Write a proposal outlining the main problems, suggesting two or three measures, and explaining the expected benefits.
items.pv: Sếp cần đề xuất cải thiện sức khoẻ tinh thần nhân viên. Viết đề xuất: vấn đề chính, 2–3 biện pháp, lợi ích dự kiến.
c: Mục đích, có tiêu đề mục
u: I would propose the following measures:
Tôi đề xuất các biện pháp sau:
Các biện pháp này có khả năng
m:
Purpose
This proposal sets out a number of practical measures to improve the wellbeing of staff in our office, following concerns raised in the recent employee survey.

Current problems
It has become apparent that many employees are experiencing high levels of stress. Over sixty percent of respondents reported regularly working beyond their contracted hours, and a similar proportion said they rarely take a proper lunch break. Sick leave has also risen by twenty percent over the past year. In interviews, several team leaders admitted that they themselves feel unable to switch off in the evenings, which inevitably sets an example for their teams. New employees, meanwhile, said they were unsure whether leaving on time would be seen as a lack of commitment.

Proposed measures
I would propose the following measures. Firstly, the company could introduce a policy discouraging emails outside working hours, except in genuine emergencies. Secondly, a quiet room could be created where staff can rest or take short breaks away from their desks. Finally, managers could receive training in recognising signs of burnout and holding supportive conversations. In addition, the company could offer each employee two flexible 'wellbeing hours' per month, which could be used for exercise, medical appointments or simply rest.

Expected benefits
These measures are likely to reduce stress and sick leave, while improving morale and productivity. They are also relatively inexpensive to implement. I would recommend reviewing their impact through a follow-up survey in six months.

items.en: Review: A Book That Changed Your Thinking
items.vi: Nhận xét một cuốn sách làm bạn thay đổi suy nghĩ
items.p: A magazine is inviting readers to review a book that changed the way they think. Write a review describing the book, explaining how it affected you, and saying whether you would recommend it.
items.pv: Viết bài nhận xét một cuốn sách làm bạn thay đổi suy nghĩ: giới thiệu, nó ảnh hưởng bạn thế nào, có nên đọc không.
c: Nó thay đổi bạn thế nào
u: At its heart, the book is about
Cốt lõi của cuốn sách là
Điều làm tôi ấn tượng nhất là
Điểm dè dặt duy nhất của tôi là
m: Few books have influenced my everyday decisions as much as 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' by the psychologist Daniel Kahneman.

At its heart, the book is about the two systems that govern how we think: one fast, intuitive and emotional, the other slow, deliberate and logical. Kahneman draws on decades of research to show how often the fast system leads us astray, from overconfidence in our predictions to irrational fears about unlikely risks. Crucially, he does not merely list errors but explains the mechanisms behind them, using simple experiments that readers can try on themselves.

What struck me most was the realisation that intelligence offers little protection against these biases. Since reading it, I have become far more cautious about first impressions, and I try to pause before making important financial or professional decisions. I have even started keeping a record of my predictions to check how accurate they really are. Perhaps most importantly, it has made me more patient with other people's mistakes, since I now recognise how naturally our minds take shortcuts.

My only reservation is that the book is long and, in places, rather dense, so it is not ideal for a quick holiday read. Nevertheless, I would wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who wants to understand why intelligent people make poor decisions, and how to avoid doing so themselves.

items.p: You work for a tour company. A customer has complained that a tour guide was late and that the hotel was not as described. Write a reply apologising, explaining what happened, and offering a solution.
items.pv: Bạn làm ở công ty du lịch. Khách khiếu nại hướng dẫn viên đến muộn và khách sạn không như mô tả. Viết thư xin lỗi, giải thích, đưa giải pháp.
c: Cảm ơn phản hồi, xin lỗi
Giải thích nguyên nhân (không đổ lỗi khách)
u: Thank you for taking the time to
Cảm ơn quý khách đã dành thời gian
Please accept our sincere apologies for
Xin quý khách nhận lời xin lỗi chân thành về
Sau khi xem xét sự việc,
m: Dear Mr Taylor,

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback about your recent tour of central Vietnam. Please accept our sincere apologies for the problems you experienced. I would also like to apologise for the fact that your first email did not receive a reply within our usual forty-eight hours.

Having looked into the matter, I can confirm that your guide was delayed by a road closure on the first morning. However, he should have informed you immediately, and I fully understand how frustrating the wait must have been. Regarding the hotel, our partner had recently changed ownership, and several of the facilities shown on our website were temporarily unavailable. We should have checked this and informed you before your arrival. Your feedback has also been shared with the guide concerned and with our hotel partnerships team, so that the lessons from your experience are applied across all our tours.
We have since updated our procedures so that guides must contact customers within ten minutes of any delay, and we now inspect all partner hotels every three months.

As a gesture of goodwill, we would like to refund thirty percent of the cost of your tour and offer you a free day trip should you visit Vietnam again. I hope this goes some way towards restoring your confidence in our company.

Yours sincerely,
Pham Lan Anh
Customer Relations Manager

items.vi: Bài luận: công nghệ và sự chú ý
items.p: "Digital technology has made us better informed but worse at thinking." Write an essay evaluating this claim.
items.pv: “Công nghệ số khiến ta biết nhiều hơn nhưng suy nghĩ kém đi.” Viết bài luận đánh giá nhận định.
c: Mở bài: diễn giải, đặt vấn đề
Phản biện: suy nghĩ kém đi / sắc thái
u: It is difficult to dispute that
Khó có thể phủ nhận rằng
Whether this has made us better thinkers, however, is
Tuy nhiên, liệu điều này có khiến ta suy nghĩ tốt hơn hay không
To attribute this solely to technology would be
Quy hết cho công nghệ là
m: It is difficult to dispute that digital technology has transformed our access to information. Facts that once required a trip to a library are now available in seconds, and specialist knowledge that was confined to universities can be found on any smartphone. In this narrow sense, we are undeniably better informed.

Whether this has made us better thinkers, however, is far less certain. Thinking well depends not merely on access to information but on the capacity to sustain attention, weigh competing claims and tolerate complexity. There is growing evidence that the fragmented, notification-driven environment of digital media erodes precisely these capacities, rewarding rapid reaction over reflection and confident assertion over careful doubt. Search engines, moreover, encourage us to outsource memory, so that we increasingly know where to find an answer without understanding it.

To attribute this solely to technology would nonetheless be simplistic. The same tools that distract us also make possible forms of collaborative inquiry that were previously unimaginable, and many people use them to think more deeply rather than less. The decisive factor appears to be not the technology itself but the habits we bring to it. Those who read long-form articles, follow arguments to their conclusion and deliberately seek out opposing views are using the same devices to very different effect. Educational systems, too, bear some responsibility for whether young people learn to do so.

What emerges, then, is a qualified agreement with the claim. Digital technology has made information abundant and attention scarce; whether we become wiser as a result depends on whether we treat that scarce attention as something worth protecting.

items.vi: Bài báo: thành phố tôi biết
items.p: A travel magazine is publishing a series called 'The City I Know', in which residents describe a side of their city that tourists rarely see. Write an article for the series.
items.pv: Tạp chí du lịch có chuyên mục “Thành phố tôi biết”: người dân kể về góc thành phố du khách ít thấy. Viết bài cho chuyên mục.
c: Một / hai góc ít người biết, miêu tả sinh động
Ý nghĩa với bạn / cộng đồng
Kết bài để lại ấn tượng
u: Hầu hết du khách thấy … nhưng ít ai
What gives the place its character is
Điều làm nơi này có hồn là
If you want to know the city,
m: Most visitors to Hanoi see the lake, the Old Quarter and the motorbikes, but few see the city before it wakes up.

At dawn, Hoan Kiem Lake belongs not to tourists but to the elderly. Groups of women in matching tracksuits practise tai chi to music from a portable speaker; a retired engineer walks backwards around the lake, convinced it improves his balance; couples in their seventies dance a slow waltz under the trees. By seven o'clock, they have gone, and the city of commerce and traffic takes their place. Nobody seems to know who organises it; it simply happens, every morning, rain or shine, as it apparently has for decades.

A few streets away, in alleys too narrow for cars, another Hanoi carries on. Neighbours share tea on tiny plastic stools, children do homework in doorways, and an old man repairs radios that nobody else would bother to fix. What gives these places their character is not architecture but intimacy: lives lived partly in public, with a generosity that the city's busy main roads rarely reveal. I have lived in one of these alleys for eleven years, and in that time I have been fed, scolded, advised and looked after by people whose names I learned only gradually. When my father was ill, it was the neighbours, not the hospital, who noticed first.

If you want to know the city, set your alarm for five, walk slowly, and accept every cup of tea you are offered. The postcard Hanoi will still be there at nine. Leave the map in your pocket and let yourself get a little lost.

items.vi: Báo cáo: chính sách làm việc từ xa
items.p: You have been asked by your company's board to evaluate the remote working policy introduced last year. Write a report assessing its effects on productivity, staff wellbeing and company culture, with recommendations.
items.pv: Hội đồng quản trị nhờ bạn đánh giá chính sách làm việc từ xa áp dụng năm ngoái: năng suất, sức khoẻ nhân viên, văn hoá công ty, và khuyến nghị.
c: Mục đích, phương pháp (có tiêu đề mục)
Sức khoẻ nhân viên và văn hoá
u: A more mixed picture emerges with regard to
Bức tranh phức tạp hơn khi xét
m:
Introduction
This report evaluates the remote working policy introduced in January, under which staff may work from home up to three days a week. It draws on performance data, a staff survey completed by 82% of employees and interviews with team leaders.

Productivity
The data suggest that overall output has remained stable, with modest improvements in departments where work is largely independent, such as software development and finance. Teams that rely heavily on collaboration, notably product design, report slower decision-making. Customer satisfaction scores, a useful indirect measure, have also remained broadly unchanged since the policy was introduced.

Wellbeing and culture
A large majority of staff value the flexibility, citing reduced commuting time and improved family life. However, a more mixed picture emerges with regard to company culture. Newer employees in particular report feeling isolated and find it harder to learn informally from experienced colleagues. Several team leaders also expressed concern about a gradual weakening of cross-departmental relationships. Attendance at voluntary company events has fallen by roughly a third, and staff turnover among employees with less than one year's service has risen slightly, although it is too early to establish a clear causal link.

Recommendations
It is therefore recommended that the policy be retained, with three adjustments. First, teams should agree on two common office days each week to support collaboration. Second, new employees should spend their first three months primarily in the office, paired with a mentor. Finally, the company should organise regular in-person events to maintain connections across departments. Progress should be reviewed after twelve months using the same indicators.

items.en: Letter to the Editor: Heritage and Development
items.vi: Thư gửi toà soạn: di sản và phát triển
items.p: A newspaper has reported plans to demolish a historic market building to make way for a shopping centre. Write a letter to the editor responding to the report and presenting a reasoned argument.
items.pv: Báo đưa tin kế hoạch phá khu chợ cổ để xây trung tâm thương mại. Viết thư gửi toà soạn phản hồi và lập luận chặt chẽ.
c: Mở thư, nêu bài báo đang phản hồi
Lập luận chính, có bằng chứng
Thừa nhận lý lẽ của phía kia
Đề xuất thay thế, kết thư
u: I read with dismay your report on
Tôi đã đọc với nỗi thất vọng bài báo về
Surely it is not beyond the wit of
Chắc chắn không ngoài khả năng của
m: Dear Editor,

I read with dismay your report on the proposal to demolish the old Dong Ba market building to make way for a shopping centre. The upper floor, with its original iron columns and tiled roof, is among the last surviving examples of its kind in central Vietnam.

It is worth recalling that the market has stood on this site, in one form or another, for well over a century. It is not merely a place of trade but a living record of the city's history, and one of the few public spaces where residents of every background still mix. Its value to tourism is equally significant: visitors come precisely to experience something that cannot be found in any shopping centre in the world.

I do not dispute that the building is in poor repair, nor that traders deserve modern facilities, safe wiring and proper drainage. The developers are right that change is needed. But demolition is not the only, or even the most economical, way of achieving it. Once the building is gone, no amount of investment will bring it back, and future generations will rightly ask why we did not pause to consider the alternatives.

Cities from Barcelona to Melbourne have restored historic markets while upgrading their infrastructure, often increasing both visitor numbers and traders' incomes. Surely it is not beyond the wit of our planners to do the same. I would urge the council to commission an independent study of restoration options before any irreversible decision is taken.

Yours faithfully,
Le Minh Quan

See you on Monday!
Linh

It was already half past eight, and the interview started at nine. I felt sick. I didn't know what to do, so I asked the woman next to me for help. Luckily, she worked near the company and told me to get off at the next stop and take a taxi with her. We shared the cost and chatted all the way. In the end, I arrived just in time, and I got the job. Now she is my colleague and one of my best friends.

items.vi: Bài báo: Nơi tôi yêu thích
items.p: You see this announcement in an English-language magazine for teenagers: “Articles wanted! Tell us about your favourite place in your town. What is it like? Why do you like it? Would you recommend it to visitors?” Write your article.
items.pv: Tạp chí tuổi teen mời viết bài: nơi bạn thích nhất ở thành phố bạn: nơi đó thế nào, vì sao thích, có nên giới thiệu cho khách không.

items.m:
A Quiet Corner in a Busy City
My favourite place in Hanoi is a small bookshop café in the Old Quarter. From the outside, it looks like an ordinary shop, but upstairs there is a peaceful room full of old books, comfortable chairs and plants.
What I love most is the calm. Outside, the streets are noisy and crowded, but inside you can read for hours with a cup of coconut coffee and nobody disturbs you. The owner is very kind and often recommends books.
If you visit Hanoi, I would definitely recommend it, especially on a hot afternoon. It is the perfect place to rest after a long day of sightseeing.

I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,

items.en: Article: Can Teenagers Live without Phones?
items.vi: Bài báo: Tuổi teen sống thiếu điện thoại được không?
items.p: Your school magazine is asking students: “Could you live without your phone for a week? What would be difficult? What might be good about it?” Write an article answering these questions.
items.pv: Báo trường hỏi: bạn có sống thiếu điện thoại một tuần được không, điều gì khó, điều gì có thể tốt.
c: Trả lời: có làm được không
items.m:
To be honest, I'm not sure I could live without my phone for a whole week, but I'd like to try.
The hardest thing would be keeping in touch with my friends. We use group chats to plan everything, from homework to weekend trips, so I would probably miss a lot. I also use my phone for music and maps, so getting around would be more difficult.
On the other hand, there could be some real benefits. I would probably sleep better, because I often look at my screen late at night. I might also read more and spend more time talking to my family.
All in all, a week without a phone would be hard, but it could be a useful experiment.

items.vi: Email xin lỗi bạn
items.p: You forgot your English friend's birthday party last Saturday. Write an email to her. Apologise, explain what happened, and suggest a way to celebrate together soon.
items.pv: Bạn quên tiệc sinh nhật của bạn người Anh hôm thứ Bảy. Viết email xin lỗi, giải thích chuyện gì đã xảy ra và đề nghị cách cùng ăn mừng sớm.
c: Giải thích chuyện đã xảy ra
u: Let me make it up to you
Mong bạn bỏ qua cho mình
m: Hi Sophie,
I'm so sorry I missed your birthday party on Saturday. I feel terrible about it.

What happened was that my grandmother was ill, so my family drove to her village on Friday night. There was no signal there, and with everything going on I completely forgot to message you. That's no excuse, though.
Let me make it up to you. Can I take you out for dinner next weekend? There's a new Korean restaurant near your house, and it's my treat. I've also got a small present for you.
Hope you can forgive me.
Love,
Mai

items.en: Essay: Should Schools Ban Mobile Phones?
items.vi: Bài luận: Trường có nên cấm điện thoại?
items.p: In your English class you have been talking about technology in schools. Now your teacher has asked you to write an essay. “Schools should ban mobile phones during the school day. Do you agree?” Notes: write about 1. concentration in lessons 2. safety and contact with parents 3. your own idea.
items.pv: Bài luận: trường có nên cấm điện thoại trong ngày học? Viết về: 1. sự tập trung 2. an toàn, liên lạc với bố mẹ 3. ý của bạn.
c: Nêu quan điểm ở mở bài
Ý 1: sự tập trung trong giờ học
Ý 2: an toàn và liên lạc với bố mẹ
Ý 3 riêng của bạn + kết luận
u: However, it could be argued that
Tuy nhiên, có thể nói rằng
items.m:
Mobile phones have become part of daily life, and many schools are now considering banning them during lessons and breaks. While a complete ban has some advantages, I believe a more flexible approach would be better.
On the one hand, phones are a major source of distraction. Notifications and games make it difficult for students to concentrate, and some teachers say that attention has fallen noticeably in recent years. Removing phones during lessons would almost certainly help.
However, it could be argued that phones are important for safety. Many parents want to be able to contact their children, especially when they travel home alone. A total ban could make families anxious.
In my view, phones can also be useful learning tools, for example for looking up words or recording presentations. On balance, I think schools should ask students to switch phones off in lessons but allow them at lunchtime, rather than banning them completely.

items.en: Review of a Film or Series
items.vi: Bài nhận xét phim / phim bộ
items.p: An international website for students is looking for reviews: “Tell us about a film or TV series that made you think. What is it about? What did you learn from it? Would you recommend it to other students?” Write your review.
items.pv: Trang web quốc tế cho học sinh mời viết nhận xét về một phim / phim bộ khiến bạn suy nghĩ: nội dung, bạn học được gì, có nên giới thiệu không.
c: Tên phim và nội dung chính
Điều khiến bạn suy nghĩ / học được
Có nên giới thiệu cho học sinh khác không
u: Điều làm tôi ấn tượng nhất là
Điểm tôi chưa thích duy nhất là
items.m:
Hidden Figures tells the true story of three African-American women who worked as mathematicians at NASA in the 1960s, during the race to send astronauts into space. The film is set at a time when they faced discrimination both as women and because of their race.
What struck me most was how much talent can be wasted when people are not given a fair chance. The women solve problems that their colleagues cannot, yet they have to fight to be allowed into meetings or even to use the same bathroom. It made me think about how many unfair rules still exist today.
The acting is excellent, and the story is told with humour as well as anger. My only criticism is that some scenes feel a little too neat, as if real history had been simplified.
Even so, I would highly recommend it to other students, especially anyone interested in science. It is inspiring, entertaining and genuinely thought-provoking.

items.vi: Báo cáo về nhà văn hoá thanh niên
items.p: The manager of your local youth centre wants to attract more young people. She has asked you to write a report describing the facilities now, explaining why some young people do not use the centre, and recommending improvements.
items.pv: Quản lý nhà văn hoá thanh niên nhờ bạn viết báo cáo: cơ sở vật chất hiện có, vì sao một số bạn trẻ không đến, và đề xuất cải thiện.
c: Tiêu đề, mục đích báo cáo
Cơ sở vật chất hiện tại
Lý do một số bạn trẻ không đến
u: The aim of this report is to
Mục đích của báo cáo này là
items.m:
Report on the Riverside Youth Centre
Introduction
The aim of this report is to describe the current facilities, explain why some young people do not use the centre, and suggest improvements. It is based on a short survey of thirty students.
Current facilities
At present, the centre has a sports hall, a small library and a room with two computers. The sports hall is popular, but the other rooms are rarely used.
Reasons for low attendance
According to the survey, many young people think the centre is old-fashioned. The computers are slow, there is no Wi-Fi, and the centre closes at six o'clock, before many students finish their extra classes.
Recommendations
I would recommend that the centre installs Wi-Fi and replaces the computers. Opening until nine o'clock on weekdays would also make a big difference. Finally, a music room or a space for clubs could attract students who are not interested in sport.

items.en: Letter of Application for a Volunteer Job
items.vi: Thư ứng tuyển tình nguyện viên
items.p: You see this advertisement: “Volunteers wanted for an international music festival. We need people to help visitors, give information and work in our information tent. Write and tell us why you would be a good volunteer.” Write your letter of application.
items.pv: Quảng cáo tuyển tình nguyện viên cho lễ hội âm nhạc quốc tế: giúp khách, cung cấp thông tin. Viết thư ứng tuyển, nói vì sao bạn phù hợp.
c: Mở thư trang trọng, nói lý do viết
Kinh nghiệm / kỹ năng liên quan
u: I am writing to apply for
Tôi viết thư để ứng tuyển
I look forward to hearing from you
m: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to apply for a position as a volunteer at your international music festival, which I saw advertised on your website.

I am a second-year tourism student, and I have experience of working with visitors. Last summer, I worked part time at a hotel reception in Hoi An, where I dealt with guests from many different countries and helped them with directions, bookings and problems. I speak English fluently and some basic Korean.

I believe I would be a good volunteer because I am patient, friendly and calm under pressure. I am also a huge fan of live music, and I would love the chance to be part of such an exciting event while gaining more experience for my future career.
I am available for the whole festival weekend and would be happy to attend any training sessions.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Thu Ha

items.en: Article: A Skill Everyone Should Learn
items.vi: Bài báo: Một kỹ năng ai cũng nên học
items.p: A magazine for young people is running a series called “Life Skills”. Write an article about one practical skill you think every young person should learn before leaving school. Explain why it is important and how young people could learn it.
items.pv: Tạp chí giới trẻ có chuyên mục Kỹ năng sống. Viết bài về một kỹ năng thực tế ai cũng nên học trước khi ra trường: vì sao quan trọng, học thế nào.
c: Tiêu đề / câu mở thu hút
items.m:
Money Matters
Have you ever reached the end of the month and wondered where all your money went? You are not alone. Surprisingly few young people leave school knowing how to manage money, yet it is one of the most useful skills anyone can have.
Learning to budget not only helps you avoid debt but also gives you freedom. If you know how much you earn and spend, you can save for things that matter to you, whether that is a trip abroad or a course you want to take. It also helps you avoid common traps, such as buying expensive things on credit.
The good news is that the basics are easy to learn. Schools could include a few lessons on budgeting and saving, and parents could involve teenagers in planning family expenses. There are also free apps that show you exactly where your money goes.
Money may not buy happiness, but knowing how to manage it can certainly prevent a lot of stress.

items.en: Essay: Is Tourism Good for Local People?
items.vi: Bài luận: Du lịch có tốt cho người dân địa phương?
items.p: Your teacher has asked you to write an essay. “Tourism brings more benefits than problems to local communities. Do you agree?” Notes: write about 1. jobs and income 2. the environment 3. your own idea.
items.pv: Bài luận: du lịch mang lại cho cộng đồng địa phương lợi nhiều hơn hại? Viết về: 1. việc làm, thu nhập 2. môi trường 3. ý của bạn.
c: Ý 1: việc làm và thu nhập
u: Một điểm khác cần xem xét là
items.m:
Tourism is one of the fastest-growing industries in the world, and many communities depend on it. Although it can cause serious problems, I believe that, if managed well, it brings more benefits than harm.
There is no doubt that tourism creates jobs. Hotels, restaurants, guides and drivers all depend on visitors, and in many rural areas tourism provides income that farming alone cannot. It can also encourage young people to stay in their home towns instead of moving to cities.
Nevertheless, tourism can damage the environment. Beaches become polluted, water is used up by hotels, and popular areas suffer from traffic and litter. Ha Long Bay, for example, has struggled with plastic waste.
Another point to consider is culture. Tourism can help preserve traditions, because visitors pay to see festivals and crafts, but it can also turn them into performances for tourists.
To sum up, tourism is beneficial overall, but only if local people are involved in decisions and the environment is protected.

items.vi: Bài luận: Đầu tư cho không gian công cộng
items.p: Your class has attended a panel discussion on how city councils should spend money to improve the quality of life. You have made the notes below. Write an essay discussing two of the options in your notes. Explain which option is more important, giving reasons. Notes: Which should receive more funding? parks and green spaces · public transport · libraries and community centres.
items.pv: Bài luận: bàn 2 trong 3 lựa chọn (công viên, giao thông công cộng, thư viện / nhà văn hoá) mà thành phố nên chi tiền; nói lựa chọn nào quan trọng hơn, có lý do.
c: Bàn lựa chọn 1 có lý do
Bàn lựa chọn 2 có lý do
Kết luận: lựa chọn nào quan trọng hơn
u: Một lý lẽ thuyết phục cho
Cân nhắc cả hai lựa chọn,
items.m:
As cities grow larger and more crowded, councils face difficult choices about where to invest limited public money. Of the options discussed, green spaces and public transport seem to me the most significant, although for rather different reasons.
A compelling argument for investing in parks is their effect on health. Green spaces encourage exercise, reduce stress and provide relief from heat in increasingly hot summers. In dense neighbourhoods, a park may be the only place where children can play safely or where older residents can meet. Unlike many facilities, parks are free and open to everyone, which makes them particularly valuable for low-income families.
Public transport, however, affects the quality of life of almost every resident every day. Reliable buses and trains reduce traffic congestion and air pollution, and they make it possible for people without cars to reach jobs, schools and hospitals. In cities where commuting can take two hours, an efficient metro line can give people back a significant part of their day.
That said, the two are not entirely separate. A park that cannot be reached easily is of limited use, and a transport system that serves only business districts does little for residents' wellbeing.
Weighing up both options, I believe public transport should receive priority, because it underpins access to everything else a city offers, including its parks. Nevertheless, councils should ensure that new transport projects are planned alongside green spaces rather than at their expense.

items.vi: Đề xuất: Cải thiện sức khoẻ tinh thần sinh viên
items.p: The principal of your college is concerned that students are under too much stress. She has asked students to submit proposals. Write a proposal describing the main causes of stress, suggesting two or three ways the college could help, and explaining how these measures would benefit students.
items.pv: Hiệu trưởng lo sinh viên quá căng thẳng. Viết đề xuất: nguyên nhân chính, 2–3 cách trường có thể giúp, và lợi ích của các biện pháp đó.
c: Tiêu đề, mục đích đề xuất
Nguyên nhân chính gây căng thẳng
Lợi ích của các biện pháp

items.m:
Proposal: Reducing Student Stress
Introduction
The purpose of this proposal is to identify the main causes of stress among students at our college and to recommend practical ways of addressing them. It is based on informal discussions with around forty students.
Main causes of stress
A major source of stress is the timing of assessments. Deadlines in different subjects frequently fall in the same week, leaving students overwhelmed. Many students also mention uncertainty about their future careers and a lack of anyone to talk to when they are struggling.
Recommendations
Firstly, it is recommended that departments coordinate their deadlines through a shared calendar, so that major assignments are spread more evenly across the term. Secondly, the college could introduce regular drop-in sessions with a trained counsellor, available without an appointment. Finally, a series of short workshops on time management and career planning would give students practical tools as well as reassurance.
Expected benefits
These measures would enable students to plan their workload more effectively and to seek help before problems become serious. Coordinated deadlines alone could significantly reduce the periods of intense pressure that students describe. In the longer term, students who feel supported are more likely to stay motivated and achieve better results.
Conclusion
The changes proposed are relatively inexpensive, and I am confident that they would make a noticeable difference to student wellbeing.

items.vi: Nhận xét: Một bảo tàng hoặc triển lãm
items.p: A cultural website has asked readers to review a museum or exhibition that tried to make history or science interesting for young people. Describe what the museum or exhibition offered, evaluate how successful it was, and say who you would recommend it to.
items.pv: Trang văn hoá mời nhận xét một bảo tàng / triển lãm làm lịch sử hoặc khoa học hấp dẫn với giới trẻ: có gì, thành công đến đâu, giới thiệu cho ai.
c: Giới thiệu bảo tàng / triển lãm
Đánh giá mức độ thành công (điểm mạnh, điểm yếu)
u: thành công đáng khen trong việc
items.m:
The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology in Hanoi sets out to introduce visitors to the country's fifty-four ethnic groups, and for the most part it succeeds admirably in bringing their cultures to life.
The museum is divided into an indoor exhibition and a large outdoor area. Inside, displays of clothing, tools and musical instruments are accompanied by short videos in which people from different communities explain their own traditions. Outside, visitors can walk into full-size traditional houses, including an impressive communal house with a roof that rises more than fifteen metres.
What makes the museum particularly effective for young people is that it avoids presenting cultures as frozen in the past. Many exhibits show how traditions are changing, for example how young people in mountain villages combine traditional festivals with social media. The outdoor houses, which visitors can explore freely, are far more engaging than objects behind glass.
Where the museum falls short is in its information panels, some of which are long, dense and poorly translated into English. Families with small children may also find that the indoor section requires more patience than their children have.
Overall, however, this is one of the most rewarding museums in the city. It would particularly appeal to teenagers and university students interested in culture or social change, and to any visitor who wants to understand Vietnam beyond its major tourist sights. Allow at least three hours, and do not miss the outdoor section.

items.vi: Thư gửi biên tập báo
items.p: A local newspaper recently published an article claiming that young people today are less willing to work hard than previous generations. Write a letter to the editor responding to the article, giving your views and supporting them with examples.
items.pv: Báo địa phương đăng bài cho rằng giới trẻ ngày nay lười hơn thế hệ trước. Viết thư gửi biên tập phản hồi, nêu quan điểm, có ví dụ.
c: Mở thư, nhắc tới bài báo
Ví dụ / lý lẽ ủng hộ
u: I am writing in response to
Tôi viết thư để phản hồi
Một ví dụ điển hình là
m: Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to the article “A Generation That Won't Work Hard”, published in last Saturday's edition. As a twenty-year-old university student, I found its conclusions both unfair and poorly supported.

While I accept that the way young people work has changed, I do not believe that this reflects a lack of effort. Many of my friends combine full-time study with part-time jobs, often in cafés or delivery work, simply to cover their living costs. A case in point is my flatmate, who studies engineering during the day and tutors secondary school students three evenings a week.

What the article describes as laziness may sometimes be a different set of priorities. Young people are more likely than previous generations to question long working hours or to leave jobs that damage their health. This is not an unwillingness to work, but a recognition that productivity and exhaustion are not the same thing. Many young people I know work longer hours than their parents did, often in jobs that offer far less security.
Finally, the article relied largely on the opinions of a few employers rather than on evidence. Generalising about millions of people on this basis seems to me irresponsible.
I would urge your readers to judge young people by what they actually do rather than by stereotypes.
Yours faithfully,
Le Bao Chau

items.en: Essay: Learning Online versus in a Classroom
items.vi: Bài luận: Học trực tuyến hay học trên lớp
items.p: Your class has watched a documentary about the future of education. Write an essay discussing whether online learning can replace learning in a classroom. Consider two of the following: cost and access · social development · quality of teaching. Give reasons for your opinion.
items.pv: Bài luận: học trực tuyến có thể thay học trên lớp không? Bàn 2 trong 3 khía cạnh: chi phí và khả năng tiếp cận · phát triển xã hội · chất lượng giảng dạy.
u: Hầu như không còn nghi ngờ
items.m:
The rapid growth of online courses has led some to predict that traditional classrooms will soon become unnecessary. While online learning offers clear advantages, I do not believe it can fully replace learning in a physical classroom, particularly for younger students.
There is little doubt that online learning has widened access to education. Students in remote areas can now attend courses taught by experts in other countries, and many courses are cheaper or free. For adults who need to study around work and family commitments, the flexibility of online learning can make the difference between studying and not studying at all.
By contrast, the social side of education is much harder to reproduce online. Schools are not only places where knowledge is transmitted; they are where young people learn to cooperate, resolve conflicts and form friendships. Video calls can support these interactions but rarely replace them, and many students who studied online during school closures reported feeling isolated and less motivated.
It is worth noting that the quality of online learning varies enormously. Well-designed courses can be excellent, but simply recording lectures and posting them online often produces passive, disengaged learners.
Ultimately, the most promising future is likely to combine both approaches, using online tools to extend access while preserving the classroom as a place for discussion, collaboration and personal support.

items.vi: Báo cáo: Chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ
items.p: Your college ran a language exchange programme last term, pairing local students with international students. The director has asked you to write a report evaluating the programme, explaining what worked well and what did not, and making recommendations for next year.
items.pv: Trường đã có chương trình trao đổi ngôn ngữ. Viết báo cáo đánh giá: điều gì tốt, điều gì chưa, đề xuất cho năm sau.
c: Tiêu đề, mục đích báo cáo
u: Một phàn nàn lặp lại là
Dựa trên các kết quả này,
items.m:
Evaluation of the Language Exchange Programme
Introduction
This report evaluates the language exchange programme run last term, in which sixty local students were paired with international students for weekly conversation sessions. It draws on an online survey completed by forty-five participants.
What worked well
Feedback suggests that the programme was valued highly. Most participants said their speaking confidence had improved, and many had formed friendships that continued outside the sessions. The monthly social events, such as the cooking evening, were especially popular and helped participants meet people beyond their own partner.
Areas for improvement
A recurring complaint was the matching process. Several pairs had very different language levels or incompatible timetables, which led some to stop meeting after a few weeks. Others felt that unstructured conversation became repetitive, and that they did not know what to talk about.
Recommendations
In light of these findings, I would recommend three changes. Firstly, participants should complete a short questionnaire on their level, interests and availability so that partners can be matched more carefully. Secondly, a list of suggested topics and short activities could be provided for each week. Finally, a mid-term check-in would allow coordinators to identify pairs that are not working and arrange new partners.
Conclusion
Overall, the programme was a success, and with these adjustments it could reach more students and maintain their participation throughout the term.

items.en: Essay: Should Museums Return Cultural Objects?
items.vi: Bài luận: Bảo tàng có nên trả lại hiện vật văn hoá?
items.p: Write an essay discussing the following question: “Should museums return objects that were taken from other countries during colonial periods?” Consider the arguments on both sides and give your own opinion.
items.pv: Bài luận: bảo tàng có nên trả lại hiện vật bị lấy từ nước khác thời thuộc địa? Bàn cả hai phía và nêu ý kiến của bạn.
c: Lý lẽ ủng hộ việc trả lại
Lý lẽ phản đối / lo ngại
Ý kiến riêng có lập luận
u: Few debates in the cultural world are as
Ít cuộc tranh luận văn hoá nào
Người ủng hộ trả lại cho rằng
Tuy nhiên, người phản đối nêu
items.m:
Few debates in the cultural world are as charged as the question of whether museums should return objects acquired during colonial rule. What was once regarded as a matter of curatorial practice is now widely seen as a question of justice.
Proponents of repatriation contend that many of these objects were taken through force, coercion or grossly unequal exchanges, and that their continued display abroad perpetuates the injustices under which they were removed. For the communities from which they came, such objects are often not merely artefacts but carriers of religious meaning, identity and memory. Returning them, on this view, is an act of acknowledgement rather than charity.
Critics, however, raise practical and philosophical objections. Some argue that major museums allow millions of visitors to encounter the art of many cultures side by side, fostering an understanding that would be lost if collections were dispersed. Others question whether the institutions now requesting objects are the rightful heirs of those from whom they were taken, given that borders and states have changed. There are also concerns, sometimes exaggerated, about the conditions in which returned objects would be preserved.
It seems to me that the strongest case lies with repatriation, at least where it can be shown that objects were taken without consent. The argument about universal access, though sincere, conveniently assumes that access should always be provided by the institutions that benefited from colonialism. Long-term loans, shared research and digital collections can preserve global access while restoring ownership. What matters most is that decisions are made in genuine partnership rather than imposed by either side.

items.en: Article: The Pleasure of Doing Nothing
items.vi: Bài báo: Niềm vui của việc chẳng làm gì
items.p: A magazine with an educated readership has invited articles for a series called “Against the Grain”, challenging a widely held belief. Write an article arguing that modern society undervalues rest and idleness.
items.pv: Tạp chí cho độc giả trí thức mời viết loạt bài “Đi ngược số đông”. Viết bài lập luận rằng xã hội hiện đại coi nhẹ việc nghỉ ngơi và nhàn rỗi.
c: Mở bài thu hút, nêu niềm tin phổ biến
Lập luận vì sao nghỉ ngơi bị coi nhẹ
Lợi ích của nghỉ ngơi / nhàn rỗi có dẫn chứng
u: We live in an age that
Thế nhưng bằng chứng cho thấy
Có lẽ điều táo bạo nhất
items.m:
In Praise of Idleness
We live in an age that treats busyness as a virtue. Asked how we are, we answer “busy” with a hint of pride, and even our leisure has become a project to be optimised: steps counted, books logged, holidays photographed. To admit to doing nothing at all, for an afternoon or a week, feels faintly shameful.
This attitude has deep roots. Industrial societies needed disciplined workers, and the moral language that grew up around work, in which idleness was a vice and productivity a duty, has outlived the factories that produced it. Today, technology extends that logic into every waking hour, so that any unoccupied moment becomes an opportunity to reply to a message or consume another piece of content.
Yet the evidence suggests that rest is not the opposite of productivity but one of its conditions. Studies of creative work repeatedly find that ideas emerge during periods of apparent inactivity, when attention is loosened and the mind is free to wander. Countries with shorter working hours are not, on the whole, less prosperous, and employees who take proper breaks tend to make fewer errors. Far from being wasted, idle time may be where some of our most valuable thinking takes place.
There is also something beyond usefulness. Rest allows us to notice our surroundings, our relationships and our own thoughts, experiences that cannot easily be measured and are therefore easily neglected.
Perhaps the most radical thing a person can do today is to sit on a bench without a phone and simply watch the afternoon pass, without feeling the need to justify it.

items.en: Report: Reducing Waste at a Festival
items.vi: Báo cáo: Giảm rác thải ở lễ hội
items.p: You helped organise a large annual music festival in your city. The organising committee has asked you to write a report on the environmental impact of this year's festival, assessing the measures taken to reduce waste and recommending further action.
items.pv: Bạn tham gia tổ chức lễ hội âm nhạc lớn. Viết báo cáo về tác động môi trường năm nay: đánh giá biện pháp giảm rác đã làm, đề xuất thêm.
c: Tiêu đề, mục đích, nguồn dữ liệu
Biện pháp đã làm và hiệu quả
items.m:
Environmental Impact of the City Music Festival
Introduction
This report assesses the environmental impact of this year's festival, focusing on waste, and recommends further measures. It draws on figures from the waste contractor and feedback from volunteers and visitors.
Measures taken
Three main initiatives were introduced. A deposit scheme for reusable cups replaced single-use plastic cups at all bars, food vendors were required to use compostable packaging, and sorting stations staffed by volunteers were placed throughout the site. The cup scheme proved largely effective: plastic waste from drinks fell by an estimated seventy per cent compared with last year, and most visitors returned their cups.
Remaining problems
Other measures were less successful. Recycling rates fell considerably short of the target, mainly because sorting stations were overwhelmed during peak hours and much compostable packaging ended up mixed with general waste. In addition, large numbers of tents were abandoned at the campsite, creating several tonnes of waste that could not be recycled.
Recommendations
It is therefore recommended that the number of sorting stations be doubled near food areas and that volunteers be scheduled according to visitor numbers rather than evenly throughout the day. A camping deposit, refunded when visitors leave with their tents, has reduced abandonment at festivals abroad and should be considered. Finally, clear signs and announcements before headline performances could remind visitors how to sort their waste.
Conclusion
This year's festival made genuine progress, but sustained investment in organisation, rather than new initiatives alone, will be needed to meet next year's targets.

items.en: Letter: Responding to a Planning Proposal
items.vi: Thư phản hồi đề án quy hoạch
items.p: Your city council plans to replace a historic covered market with a shopping centre and car park. Write a letter to the council expressing your views on the plan, considering its likely impact on residents and businesses and proposing an alternative.
items.pv: Thành phố định thay chợ cổ có mái bằng trung tâm thương mại và bãi đỗ xe. Viết thư cho thành phố nêu quan điểm, tác động tới dân và tiểu thương, đề xuất phương án khác.
c: Mở thư, nêu lý do viết
Tác động tới cư dân và tiểu thương
u: I am writing to express my concern about
Tôi viết thư để bày tỏ lo ngại về
A more balanced approach would be
Một cách cân bằng hơn là
m: Dear Councillors,

I am writing to express my concern about the proposal to demolish the Central Covered Market and replace it with a shopping centre and multi-storey car park. While I recognise the need to modernise the area, I believe the plan in its current form would do considerable harm.

The market is not simply a building. For more than a century it has supported dozens of small family businesses, many of which could not afford the rents typically charged in shopping centres. It is also one of the few places in the city where residents of all ages and incomes still meet in the course of their daily lives. Replacing it with national chain stores would remove a source of affordable fresh food and weaken the character that draws visitors to the old town.

It would be regrettable if the council's legitimate concerns about the market's poor condition and limited parking led to the loss of something that cannot be recreated. A more balanced approach would be to restore the existing structure, improve its facilities and lighting, and create parking on the underused site to the north. The upper level of the market could be leased to cafés or small creative businesses, generating income without displacing current traders.
I trust that the council will consult traders and residents fully before making a final decision, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to that discussion.
Yours faithfully,
Pham Duc Huy

items.en: Review: A Book That Changed Your Mind
items.vi: Nhận xét: Cuốn sách làm bạn đổi suy nghĩ
items.p: A literary website invites reviews of books that changed the reviewer's mind about an important subject. Write a review describing the book, explaining how it changed your thinking, and evaluating its strengths and weaknesses.
items.pv: Trang văn học mời nhận xét cuốn sách làm bạn đổi cách nghĩ về một vấn đề quan trọng: giới thiệu, nó thay đổi bạn thế nào, điểm mạnh và yếu.
c: Giới thiệu sách và vấn đề
Bạn đã nghĩ gì trước đó và thay đổi ra sao
Điểm yếu và đánh giá chung
items.m:
Factfulness, by Hans Rosling, sets out to show that most of us hold a far gloomier view of the world than the evidence justifies. Written with his son and daughter-in-law, it draws on decades of data on health, poverty and education.
I had always assumed, like most of the people Rosling surveyed, that extreme poverty was increasing and that the world was divided into rich and poor countries with little in between. The book demolishes both assumptions. Using clear charts, Rosling shows that the proportion of people living in extreme poverty has fallen dramatically and that most of the world's population now lives in middle-income countries. Reading it, I realised that my view of the world had been shaped by images and headlines rather than by numbers.
What is most persuasive is not the statistics themselves but Rosling's analysis of why we misjudge them. He identifies a series of mental habits, such as our tendency to notice dramatic events and to assume that trends will continue in a straight line, and illustrates each with memorable stories from his career as a doctor.
Its chief weakness is perhaps a tendency to understate problems that are genuinely getting worse. Critics have argued that its optimism can sound complacent when applied to climate change or inequality within countries, and the book sometimes seems more interested in correcting pessimism than in examining these risks.
Even so, it is an unusually valuable book: humane, engaging and, above all, a lesson in thinking more carefully before deciding what we know.

items.en: Essay: Is Expertise Losing Its Authority?
items.vi: Bài luận: Chuyên gia có đang mất uy tín?
items.p: Write an essay discussing the view that expert opinion has lost its authority in the age of the internet. Consider the reasons for this change, its consequences, and how trust in expertise might be rebuilt.
items.pv: Bài luận: ý kiến chuyên gia có đang mất uy tín trong thời internet? Bàn nguyên nhân, hệ quả và cách xây lại lòng tin.
c: Mở bài nêu vấn đề và quan điểm
Cách xây dựng lại lòng tin + kết luận
u: Part of the explanation lies in
Một phần lý do nằm ở
The consequences are far from trivial
Xây lại lòng tin sẽ cần
items.m:
It has become commonplace to claim that we live in an era in which expertise counts for little, and in which the opinion of a scientist carries no more weight online than that of an anonymous commentator. The reality is more nuanced, but there is undoubtedly a crisis of trust in some areas, and its causes deserve careful examination.
Part of the explanation lies in the internet itself. Access to vast amounts of information has given many people the impression that they can evaluate complex questions without specialised training, while algorithms tend to reward content that provokes strong emotions rather than content that is accurate. Experts have also contributed to the problem. Highly publicised failures, such as inaccurate economic forecasts, and a tendency to communicate in inaccessible language have encouraged the suspicion that expert opinion is either unreliable or self-serving.
The consequences are far from trivial. When public health advice is treated as just another opinion, vaccination rates can fall and preventable diseases return. More broadly, a society that cannot agree on basic facts finds it increasingly difficult to debate what should be done about them.
Rebuilding trust will require effort on several fronts. Experts need to explain not only their conclusions but also their uncertainties, since overconfidence that is later exposed does lasting damage. Educational systems could do more to teach how knowledge is produced and tested. Above all, trust is earned through consistency and openness rather than demanded on the basis of credentials. Expertise has not lost its value; what it has lost is the assumption that its value is self-evident.
